newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. not worried over further Dow drop -- Japan EPA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. not worried over further Dow drop -- Japan EPA.

text.p: The United States is not worried about the possibility of further plunges in the New York stock market, Economic Planning Agency chief Taro Aso was quoted telling Japanese cabinet ministers on Tuesday.

"The U.S. economy is not overheating, their economy is not bad...people there (in the United States) are not worried that plunges (in the stock market) will continue," government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama quoted Aso as saying.

Aso was responding to a query from Kabun Muto, head of Management and Coordination Agency, about his trip to the United States in early August, Kajiyama said. Aso was in Washington to attend a regular Japan-U.S. economic conference.

On Friday, the Dow Jones industrial average had its biggest percentage drop in nearly six years, but rebounded on Monday to finish the day's trade at 7,803.36, up 108.70 points from Friday's 247-point decline. - Tokyo newsroom (813) 3432-8018
